thread:
Alex K: Quick sync — running a security-conscious POC with FinCorp next week. Customer wants Redwood Private deployed into their AWS account but they need guidance on whether to use VPC Peering or PrivateLink for model traffic. Their constraints: no internet egress from app subnets, TLS inspection in perimeter, and source IP must be preserved for audit logs.

Maya S: Is source-IP preservation a hard requirement or just preferred? If it's hard, PrivateLink won't preserve client source IPs by default (NLB preserves, ALB does not).

Alex K: It's hard — compliance team's asking for the originating IP in our logs. They also insist on minimal firewall rules (whitelist-only).

Raj P: Quick notes from infra:
- VPC Peering preserves source IPs and is low-latency but requires routing between the two VPCs and full route table entries.
- AWS PrivateLink (Interface endpoints) terminates to ENIs in the consumer VPC; source shows as the endpoint ENI IP unless we front with an NLB in the provider VPC (we control the provider side).
- For strict no-internet egress, PrivateLink is nice because traffic never leaves AWS backbone.

Sophie L: For Redwood Private we can offer two patterns:
1) PrivateLink with a provider-side NLB -> preserves client IPs in the NLB target group (we can share NLB IPs/ENIs for allowlisting).
2) VPC Peering + route table entries -> straight L3 routing, preserves IPs, but customer must accept cross-account peering and add specific route rules.

Maya S: Firewall snippet the customer can paste into their NGFW (high level):
```
Allow outbound TCP 443 to VPCE endpoints: vpce-*.amazonaws.com
Allow outbound TCP 1025-65535 ephemeral (if using NLB backend)
DNS UDP/UDP 53 to resolver
```
They asked for concrete IP ranges for allowlist — can we give them stable CIDRs?

Alex K: They need stable CIDRs for a security appliance that only accepts CIDR ranges. Sophie, do we publish static egress ranges for Private?

Sophie L: We don't publish a single static /16 for every customer. For PrivateLink we can provide the NLB Elastic IPs (if we allocate EIPs to the NLB). Option: we can allocate a small set of EIPs per customer (recommended for regulated customers) and share those as a whitelist. If they want VPC Peering, they only need to allow the customer's VPC CIDR on their firewall (no public IPs).

Raj P: Operational notes:
- If you want mutual TLS or mTLS between app and Redwood, we can enable client cert auth on our side.
- For TLS inspection appliances in front of the app, confirm they will not terminate TLS to the Redwood endpoint unless they re-encrypt with SNI intact. We rely on SNI for routing to model variants.

Maya S: Customer also asked about split-horizon DNS — they'll use private hosted zone to resolve redwood service names to the VPCE interface IPs. Works fine, just confirm our DNS names: `private-api.redwood-inference.svc` (they will map to ENI IPs).

Alex K: Good. Pricing Q: they wanted to understand any EIP or NLB cost if we allocate EIPs per customer. Can we give an estimate?

Sophie L: Rough ballpark: additional ~$20-25/month per EIP + per-hour NLB cost (~$0.022 per hour) and data processing charges. For a small POC we usually allocate 2 EIPs (HA across AZs) — so expect ~ $60/month in infra overhead. We'll add that as a line item to the quote.

Raj P: Preflight checklist for Solutions to hand to customer netops:
- Confirm chosen pattern: PrivateLink+NLB (recommended for no-internet) OR VPC Peering (recommended for simple L3).
- Provide us the customer VPC CIDR and list of AZs if peering.
- If PrivateLink: decide whether customer will create the Interface Endpoint or we will (we can accept either).
- If whitelisting EIPs: exchange fqdn -> EIP list (we'll provide once EIPs allocated).
- Open outbound 443 from app subnets to the ENI IPs / EIPs.

Maya S: One blocker — their security team forbids cross-account peering. That rules out VPC Peering. They will accept PrivateLink only if we can supply dedicated EIPs.

Alex K: Ok action items:
- Sophie: confirm whether we can assign 2 EIPs for the POC and an estimated monthly line item (Sophie: reply here).
- Raj: prepare a short network diagram (customer VPC -> VPCE -> NLB -> Redwood Private) and the minimal ACL/SG rules.
- Maya: I'll update the quote with the extra infra line and ask security to sign off once EIPs are provided.

Sophie L: I can do the EIPs for the POC. I'll allocate two EIPs, give you IPs by EOD, and draft the one-page network diagram + SG rules.

net-bot: [auto] Ticket NET-4521 created (customer: FinCorp POC) — assigned to Sophie L.

Alex K: Perfect. If anything changes on the customer's side (e.g., TLS inspection forcing SNI strip), flag immediately — that will require a different approach (mutual TLS or running a transit proxy). :thumbsup:
